limitations: Analyst-defined allocation, not a validated estimate of repairs, avoided emissions, investigation value, cost or future leakage. One slot assumes one source investigation; actual effort differs.

All strategies share the same linked-observation pool and hard quotas. Flux/recurrence baselines are application-defined, not the official UNEP Top 50 ranking. Breadth uses a greedy heuristic, not a guaranteed coverage optimum.

Tied midrank percentiles are relative to the filtered pool. Missing flux gives no magnitude ranking points; it is not an observed zero. Reported standard deviations are retained, not converted into confidence intervals or benefit probabilities.

Historical observations are discontinuous. Missing later records do not establish zero emissions; source feedback does not prove repair. No sums of discrete kg/h observations are interpreted as avoidable emissions.

Distinct observation dates depend on sampling opportunities and satellite coverage. They are not standardized leakage frequencies or UNEP persistency. Median source flux summarizes selected source medians, not a combined emission rate.

Sensitivity changes analyst assumptions on this same snapshot. It is not model validation or a scientific uncertainty interval. Unknown country is one quota bucket; unknown geography never increases coverage.

Unsigned replay and checksum detect changes relative to a trusted digest, not authentic data origin or physical truth. Review evidence before publishing an authorized audit. No work has been assigned or message sent.

limitations: A human determination based on submitted reference metadata; no model was called and document contents were not uploaded.
The rules check reference kind, dates and declared event/recipient/action relationships. Optional publisher retrieval records origin and bytes, not document truth or physical mitigation.
The authenticated reviewer states that the source material was inspected; this is not an independently certified inspection.
References and free-text assessment remain private. No third-party report or quotation is reproduced.
A public redacted summary is available only with explicit consent; reviewer attestation and conflict declarations are not independent identity or independence certification.
Missing later observations do not establish zero emissions. Feedback and receipts do not establish a repair or reduced emissions.
Priority is an uncalibrated investigation aid, not a physical leak likelihood or future-flux forecast.
The calibrated recurrence estimate predicts another linked MARS archive record within 365 days for a source already observed; it does not predict methane presence, emissions, repair, or mitigation.
The observed flux trend summarizes discrete detection dates only; it is not extrapolated and is not a future forecast.
A descriptive trend is emitted only with four or more numeric dates spanning at least 90 days; the method summarizes dated flux with a median pairwise Theil–Sen slope.
Observation coverage varies by sensor, revisit schedule, geography, and cloud conditions; missing observations do not mean zero emissions.
Source notification and feedback metadata do not verify recipient, repair, or emissions reduction.
This small curated casebook has not been independently validated as a predictive model.
